newsitem.title: UK: BBC Radio extends gains against commercial rivals.
newsitem.headline: BBC Radio extends gains against commercial rivals.

text.p: Britain's BBC British Radio extended its lead over commercial radio competitors in the 1996 fourth quarter, winning 49.6 percent of the listening audience against 48.3 percent for commercial stations, a radio trade group reported on Thursday.

The BBC's five radio stations and Britain's growing number of commercial stations have been locked in a sharp war for listeners, with the balance of power shifting back and forth between the two over the last year.
BBC Radio's fourth quarter figures showed a slight improvement over its third quarter performance, when it claimed 48.9 percent of UK radio listeners against 48.8 percent for commercial stations.
In the 1995 fourth quarter commercial radio had held the edge, claiming a 49.78 percent audience share against 47.2 percent for the BBC stations.
Except for its Radio One pop music station, all the BBC radio stations increased audience share for the 1996 fourth quarter, the industry research body Rajar said.
Radio 1 lost breakfast show listeners following the departure of controversial disc jockey Chris Evans, Rajar said.

Sue Farr, controller of marketing for BBC Broadcast, said the number of Radio One listeners had dropped after Evans quit in January. Evans left the BBC because it would not allow him to work a four-day week.

"The (breakfast) show did record a slight loss of 90,000 listeners quarter on quarter," she said. Rajar did not give a breakdown of audience figures for individual shows but industry estimates suggest that Evans' show pulled in about seven million listeners a week.

Farr said Radio One's audience share rose to 12.4 percent in the 1996 fourth quarter from 12 percent a year-ago. But the number of listeners tuning in to Radio One at the weekends fell to 10.7 million from 11.2 million in the previous quarter.

Despite its slippage against BBC Radio, commercial stations said they are winning the listeners prized by advertisers. Paul Brown chief executive of the Commercial Radio Companies Association said that while the BBC is 1.3 per cent ahead in audience share, commercial radio "continues to dominate listening among those target groups that advertisers are most interested in speaking to.

"Around 90 percent of all radio a advertising is targeted at people under the age of 55," Brown said. "Commercial radio reaches two-thirds of this group each week and accounts for almost 60 percent of their total radio listening."
